transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I'm here because... I hope this doesn't sound silly, but people keep acting like I'm just imagining things. And I don't want to be a bother, but I know the hospital people and some folks from the cleaning agency where I work have been watching our house. They've been keeping an eye on my cleaning routes, too. 

I know they're just trying to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. Which I am, I really am doing my best for him and keeping everything nice and clean. Is it okay that I came in to talk about that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, because it's been a little stressful having them check up on me like that.
Have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?

Oh, um... well, I don't want to sound like I'm making things up, and I know it probably sounds a little strange. I hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying this, but... sometimes, yes. 

It's usually when the house is perfectly quiet. I'll be in the kitchen, and... I hear this woman's voice. It sounds like it's coming from right near the kitchen window. It's so clear, Doctor, just as clear as if she were standing right next to me. She usually tells me to go check the locks on the doors, or she tells me I need to move my husband's pills to a different spot. 

I always listen to her, just to be safe, because I really am trying to take good care of him. That's okay, isn't it? To just listen and make sure everything is secure? I just... I don't think anyone else hears her, but she's definitely there. Does that make sense?
How long have you been hearing this voice and feeling like you are being watched?

Oh, um... gosh. I hope you aren't upset with me for not coming in sooner. I really didn't want to make a fuss or... or seem like I couldn't handle things, you know? 

But, um... I guess the voice, and knowing that people are keeping an eye on us... it's been happening for about 11 months now. Almost a year. I really hope I didn't do the wrong thing by waiting to talk about it. I just wanted to keep everything peaceful at home and not be a burden to anyone, especially since I can still do all my cleaning work just fine. 

That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope it's alright that I waited that long to tell a doctor.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep up with your daily chores or your personal hygiene over the past year?

Oh, um... well... I try so hard to keep everything perfectly nice, I really do. I hope you know that. I take my job very seriously. 

But... well, I guess things have been a little bit harder lately. I hope you don't think poorly of me, but the agency... they actually took away my supervisory routes. They said... well, some clients and coworkers mentioned they couldn't rely on my work quite the way they used to. I didn't mean to let anyone down, I promise. I just... I get so distracted making sure everything is safe. 

And at home... well, I'm still trying my best with my husband. But my pastor and my husband, they've had to step in a bit more. They said I wasn't keeping up with the caregiving and the chores safely enough. I feel terrible about it, really I do. I don't want to be a burden to them. It's just been a bit overwhelming with everything going on. That doesn't make me a bad wife or employee, does it? I'm still trying my hardest.
When you are speaking with others, do you find that your thoughts sometimes get jumbled or that people have trouble following what you are trying to say?

Oh, um... I hope you don't think I'm doing it on purpose, because I really do try to speak clearly. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

But, well... sometimes, when I'm trying to explain what's happening, I guess my mind just goes a little faster than my mouth. I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then... well, then I'll think about the church schedule, and then somehow I'm talking about the numbers on my client list for work. 

I don't mean to be confusing, I promise. It all makes sense in my head, but my husband and my pastor... they say they can't always follow me. They get a little frustrated, I think. I feel so bad when it happens. I just want to be helpful and clear. It's okay if my thoughts get a little jumbled sometimes, isn't it? I'm sure lots of people have trouble finding the right words when they're stressed, right?

Have there been times recently where you have found yourself acting in a way that seemed strange or unusual to other people, such as standing still for a very long time or doing things that didn't seem to have a clear purpose?

Oh, um... gosh. I really hope I haven't been acting too strangely. I don't want anyone to think I'm losing my mind or being difficult on purpose. I just... I like things to be tidy, you know? Being a housekeeper, it's just in my nature to want things organized. 

But... well, I suppose my husband did mention something the other day. I hope you don't think it's too weird, but sometimes at work, or even at home, I... I catch myself lining up the cleaning bottles, or the towels, or even the chairs. I have to put them in certain patterns. And then I'll walk back through the rooms over and over again. 

I know it probably looks a bit odd, but it just feels so wrong to leave them any other way. It's like an itch I have to scratch to make sure everything is perfectly in its place. It's not a bad thing to be a little extra careful with organizing, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job.

When you talk about these difficult experiences, do you find that your feelings or the way you express your emotions have changed, such as feeling like your emotions are 'flat' or not matching the situation?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I haven't come across as cold or anything like that. I try very hard to be polite and warm with everyone, especially my clients and my husband. 

I mean, I still smile when things are happy, and I definitely cry when I'm upset... probably more than I should, honestly. I always want to make sure people know I care about them. I haven't noticed my feelings going flat or anything. I'm just a normal, caring person, you know? It's good to be in touch with your emotions, right? I hope you can see that I'm trying to be as open and honest with you as I can be.
Aside from the organizing you mentioned, have there been any times where you have felt completely frozen, unable to move or speak for a period of time?

Oh, goodness, no. I hope you don't think I'm getting that bad. I would never want to just... freeze up like that. I have too much to do, you know? With work and keeping the house nice for my husband, I have to keep moving. 

I've never been unable to speak or move, I promise. I always try to stay busy and helpful. Sometimes I might pause for a moment just to think about what room I need to clean next, but that's just normal planning, right? Everyone stops to think for a second. But being completely frozen? No, I've never done anything like that. I'm doing okay in that regard, aren't I?
Over the past year, have you noticed that you have become less interested in socializing or spending time with friends and family than you used to be?

Oh, no, not at all. I really hope I don't give the impression that I'm pulling away from people or anything like that. I would hate for my family to think I don't want to be around them. 

I mean, between my housekeeping jobs and making sure my own home is taken care of for my husband, I stay pretty busy, so maybe I don't go out to big parties or anything... but I still really enjoy seeing people. I always make sure to chat with my clients, and I call my sister every week. I would never want to be rude or ignore anyone. 

It's so important to be a good friend and a good wife, don't you agree? I really do try my best to stay connected and be there for the people I care about. That's a healthy way to be, right? I hope you think I'm doing okay with that.
